chapter.title: Check! Check! (Weight and Capacity)
chapter.tagline: Verifying household weight estimates, balancing scales, and measuring liquid capacity
chapter.overview: Anu inspects the recorded weights of furniture and groceries in her house, correcting absurd measurements (like an iron almirah marked 40 g instead of 40 kg!). Students explore pan balances, standard metric weights, and measuring liquid volumes with graduated cylinders.

sections.title: Anu's Estimation Checklist: Grams vs. Kilograms
sections.subtitle: Developing realistic intuition for mass in everyday objects

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at this sheet! It says our heavy iron almirah weighs 40 grams! A packet of potato chips is 40 grams—the almirah must be 40 kilograms!

concept.heading: Distinguishing Grams (g) and Kilograms (kg)
concept.keyRule: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Light objects (spices, coins, stamps) are measured in grams; heavy objects (people, furniture, sacks of grain) in kilograms.

sections.title: The Pan Balance: Balancing Weights
sections.subtitle: Equivalence and algebraic balancing with metric weights

storyNarrative.dialogue: If we place 1 kg on the left pan, how many 250 g packets of butter must we place on the right pan to balance the beam?

concept.heading: Pan Balance Equilibrium
concept.keyRule: The balance beam rests horizontal when Left Mass = Right Mass (1,000 g = 4 × 250 g).

sections.title: Liquid Capacity: Millilitres and Litres
sections.subtitle: Measuring medicine spoons, juice cups, and water buckets

storyNarrative.dialogue: My medicine syrup spoon holds 5 millilitres, but our bucket holds 15 litres! 1 litre holds 1,000 millilitres!

concept.heading: Metric Capacity Conversion
concept.keyRule: 1 Litre (L) = 1,000 Millilitres (mL). Volume of liquids is quantified in litres and fractions thereof.
